articles.title: Klipper 0.13 released
articles.summary: Klipper 0.13 brings input shaper improvements, a new bed mesh algorithm and faster startup.
articles.text:
Klipper 0.13 is out.

Highlights:
- Input shaper calibration now runs both axes in one pass.
- The new bed mesh algorithm needs fewer probe points for the same accuracy.
- Startup on slow hosts is up to 40 % faster.

Upgrade notes: run a full firmware rebuild on every MCU after updating.

articles.title: Drying PETG: what actually works
articles.summary: We dried PETG at four temperatures and measured stringing. 65 °C for four hours wins.
articles.text:
PETG absorbs moisture faster than PLA. Wet PETG strings, pops and loses strength.

We dried four spools at 50, 55, 65 and 70 °C. At 65 °C for four hours the stringing test was clean; 70 °C started to deform the spool.

Store dried spools in a sealed box with fresh desiccant.

articles.title: Outdoor parts: PETG, ASA or PLA?
articles.summary: A year on the balcony: PLA warped, PETG and ASA held up. ASA kept its colour best.
articles.text:
We left test brackets on a south-facing balcony for a year.

PLA softened in summer and warped. PETG kept its shape but faded slightly. ASA kept shape and colour, but needs an enclosure to print well.

articles.title: Release notes: energy dashboard and voice
articles.summary: The new release adds a reworked energy dashboard, timers on more satellites and faster Assist.
articles.text:
This release reworks the energy dashboard with per-device consumption and a solar forecast.

Assist satellites can now run several named timers, and wake word detection is faster on low-power devices.

articles.title: Building a voice satellite for the kitchen
articles.summary: A step-by-step build of a small voice satellite with a good microphone and speaker.
articles.text:
A kitchen satellite needs a microphone that copes with noise. We used a dual-mic board, a 3 W speaker and a 3D printed case.

Place it away from the extractor hood and test the wake word with the tap running.
